additions.reason: The teaching's explicit conclusion — 'נמצא שנתקבצו שלשה ראשים יחד' (three heads gather together) — names the compound concept of the three-headed gathering as an independent conceptual entity. While the three individual ראשים (הצדיק, ראש השנה, מחו ודעתו) are each in the dataset as separate nodes, the teaching treats 'שלשה ראשים' as a distinct bechina-level category: the act of their convergence is itself the spiritual significance of traveling to the Tzaddik on Rosh Hashanah. This compound node is not merely a sum — it names a qualitatively different spiritual reality. It belongs in Package 1.

duplicate_edges_found.note: This edge appears twice in the dataset (edges 2 and 3 at lines 45774–45794). Both are identical. This is a data duplication, not a separate relationship.

analysis_notes.source_text_notes: Torah 94 is an extremely brief reported teaching — Reb Nosson heard only fragments of the full Torah. The text explicitly names three bechinot of ראש: (1) הצדיק — 'כִּי הַצַּדִּיק הוּא בְּחִינַת רֹאשׁ, כִּי הוּא רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל'; (2) ראש השנה — 'וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא גַם כֵּן בְּחִינַת רֹאשׁ, כִּי הוּא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה'; (3) מחו ודעתו — 'וְכָל אֶחָד בָּא עִם מֹחוֹ וְדַּעְתּוֹ לְהַצַּדִּיק... שֶׁזֶּהוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּחִינַת רֹאשׁ'. All three are in the dataset. No evil polarity is introduced — this Torah presents no opposing force. The compound concept 'שלשה ראשים' as the name for their convergence is the only gap identified.
analysis_notes.evil_mirror_check: No evil polarity exists in this Torah. The teaching describes a purely positive phenomenon — the spiritual convergence of three holy 'heads' on Rosh Hashanah. There is no evil counterpart discussed, and the text explicitly notes it is an incomplete fragment ('לא זכיתי לקבלה' — I did not merit to receive it). Any evil mirror that may have existed in the full Torah was not transmitted.
